finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes attacker-controlled base64 data to Marshal.load, enabling arbitrary object instantiation and likely remote code execution via a gadget chain.

trace.note: POST /restore route registered with no authentication or route condition
params[:state] base64-decoded and passed directly to Marshal.load
Deserialized object's .inspect is returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: None present: no authentication, no HMAC/signature on state, no class allow-list, no size limit, no content-type check. Rack::Protection does not cover request-body deserialization. Gem set unknown (no Gemfile/lockfile), so a usable gadget chain is not verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 registers POST /restore with no authentication or route condition. app.rb:6 passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight to Marshal.load with no signature, class allow-list, size limit, or content-type check. app.rb:7 returns state.inspect to the caller. Nothing else in app.rb sits between the request and the deserialization.
verdict.reason: Anonymous POST to /restore (app.rb:5) reaches Marshal.load on attacker-controlled base64 (app.rb:6) with no effective control, so untrusted deserialization is confirmed. Whether this yields code execution depends on available gadget classes, which the code here cannot show, but the unsafe sink itself is confirmed.

finding.claim: POST /import reflects attacker-chosen JSON object keys unescaped into an HTML response, enabling reflected XSS on the app origin via a cross-site text/plain form submission.
finding.source: JSON object key names in the request body read at app.rb:11 (request.body.read)
finding.sink: data.keys.join(",") returned as response body at app.rb:12, served as text/html by Sinatra default

trace.note: POST /import route registered with no CSRF token or auth
Raw body parsed with JSON.parse; Content-Type not checked, so a text/plain form body can carry JSON
Keys joined with commas and returned unescaped as the response body

finding.guards_checked: No HTML escaping on the path. Rack::Protection X-XSS-Protection header does not prevent reflection and is ignored by modern browsers. No CSRF token. No Content-Type validation. Exploitability not run; depends on browser delivery via auto-submitted text/plain form and on the endpoint being reachable from a browser.

verdict.guard_found: No HTML escaping, auth, or Content-Type check in app.rb:10-12. The one candidate control is Sinatra's default Rack::Protection middleware (not in this directory; it is not pinned, since there is no Gemfile). Its RemoteToken check may reject cross-site POSTs whose Referer host differs, but that is unconfirmed here, and the candidate's guards_checked did not consider it.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: POST /import at app.rb:10 has no auth, app.rb:11 parses the raw body without a Content-Type check, and app.rb:12 returns attacker-chosen keys unescaped, which Sinatra serves as text/html. Whether a cross-site text/plain form can reach that handler depends on Sinatra's default Rack::Protection (RemoteToken/Referer check) and the framework version, and neither is in the available code, so exploitability can't be decided here.
